newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Atlas Copco H1 report cheers market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Atlas Copco H1 report cheers market.

text.p: Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco AB cheered the market with a higher than expected six-month profit on Wednesday and repeated its forecast for a slightly higher profit in 1997 than in 1996.
Analysts welcomed the result and said they planned to lift their profit estimates for the full year.
"The group shows clearly better margins and a sharply higher order intake," said an analyst who declined to be named.
"The report shows the company has seen an expected improvement of market trends and that we still have the large upturn ahead of us, which we will see when Germany starts picking up."
Atlas Copco said profit after financial items rose 10 percent to 1.72 billion crowns in the first half of the year compared to a year ago and against market expectations of 1.55 billion.

"Despite the initial negative effect of the Prime Service acquisition, our previous forecast of a somewhat higher profit compared to 1996 stands firm," the company said, referring to the $900 million purchase of a U.S. rental equipment group.

Analysts said the report would cause them to upgrade their full year estimates. Before the report, market expectations targeted a 1997 profit of 3.21 billion crowns compared to 3.07 billion crowns in 1996.
Some analysts still saw the share as expensive.
"We will keep 'sell' on it. It has a very high valuation," said Mats Larsson at Swedbank.
Atlas Copco's share rose ahead of the report and at 1340 GMT was trading five crowns higher at 239 crowns on the Stockholm Stock Exchange from Tuesday's close but off morning highs of 244 crowns.

Although the group said it expected demand to remain at the present level for the rest of the year, it posted a 14 percent increase in order intake to 14.83 billion crowns in the first six months and sales advanced 11 percent to 13.78 billion.
Foreign exchange moves, mainly a stronger dollar, boosted both orders and sales by six percent.

The company noted significant order increases in Japan, China, Australia, South America, southern Europe and Britain while sales of compressors, advanced industrial power tools and mining equipment showed volume increases.

The operating margin rose to 12.4 percent in the first half of the year from 12 percent in a year earlier and to 13 percent in the second quarter from 12 in the first quarter, lifted by larger volumes and foreign exchange moves.
The group's largest business area, Compressor Technique, was the star performer with operating margins rising to 18 percent in the second quarter from 16 percent in the first.
"Stronger volumes in Industrial Technique and Compressor Technique and a better margin at Compressor Technique lifted profits more than expected," Larsson at Swedbank said.

Compressor Technique posted second quarter sales of 3.28 billion crowns, compared to 2.81 billion in the first quarter, while Industrial Technique's sales rose to 2.36 billion crowns from 2.14 billion.
The second quarter was strong in general with total sales of 7.38 billion crowns, up from 6.34 billion crowns in the second quarter of 1996 and from 6.41 billion in the first quarter of this year.
Profit after financial items rose 29 percent to 984 million crowns in the second quarter from a year ago and from 735 million crowns in the first quarter of 1997.
